one_line: An 11-second Hebrew how-to from a speech-language pathologist showing, with stacked text and arrows over a filmed TV, how to set a cartoon (Paw Patrol) to 0.75 playback speed for slower, 'brain-friendlier' content.

hook.visual: Locked-off vertical phone shot of a wall-mounted TV above a wooden console showing the Paw Patrol cartoon (Nick Jr style logo visible top right of the screen). Frame 0.0 s has no text; the question appears at 1.0 s over a close-up of the Paw Patrol badge.
hook.on_screen_text: ידעת שאפשר להפוך סדרות מצוירות לטובות יותר לילד שלך? (Did you know you can turn cartoons into better ones for your child?) then at 2.0 s: בפעולה פשוטה! (With a simple action!)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Inferred: the first image is a cartoon character parents of toddlers instantly recognise, and the text names the parent's own situation (the child watching cartoons) and promises a fix with 'a simple action', so the gap is open within 1 s. The question is self-contained, so no setup is needed before the promise.

beats.observed: Wall TV playing Paw Patrol (a boy character pointing at a row of badges); no overlay text yet.
Close-up of the Paw Patrol shield badge, then the pup group on a blue background. Rounded white text bubbles overlay the shot.
beats.on_screen_text: ידעת שאפשר להפוך סדרות מצוירות לטובות יותר לילד שלך? (Did you know you can turn cartoons into better ones for your child?) / בפעולה פשוטה! (With a simple action!)

beats.observed: Camera shows the TV now displaying a video-app interface with thumbnails at the bottom. Text appears at the top of the frame.
beats.on_screen_text: תורידו מהירות צפיה ⬇️ (Lower the viewing speed)

beats.observed: Settings menu opens on the TV with the Paw Patrol logo in a small preview window. Stacked text bubbles with left arrows are added one by one: first one pointing at the menu, then one at the speed row, then one at the 0.75 option. The speed list rows are too small to read confidently [unclear].
beats.on_screen_text: כנסו להגדרות ⬅️ (Go into settings) / מהירות ⬅️ (Speed) / העבירו ל0.75 ⬅️ (Switch to 0.75)

beats.observed: Back to full-screen cartoon: Marshall and Skye standing in a desert scene. A white bubble with a green check mark replaces the steps.
beats.on_screen_text: תוכן איטי יותר= (Slower content =) / ✅תוכן בריא יותר למוח ולקשב של הילד שלך (healthier content for your child's brain and attention)

beats.observed: Same desert shot with a yellow arrow pointing down at the Skye character; text bubbles at top and bottom.
beats.on_screen_text: הפירוט המלא למטה (Full details below) / מוזמנים לעקוב לתכנים נוספים ⬇️ (Invited to follow for more content)

payoff: The full how-to (settings, speed, 0.75) is complete by about 7 s; the 'why' claim (slower content = healthier for brain and attention) lands at 8 s; details deferred to the caption at 10 s.
cta: Follow for more content, and read the full details in the caption (the caption lists the same steps plus caveats). No comment or save prompt in the video.
share_or_comment_trigger: Inferred: parents send it to a partner or parent group because it is a free, 10-second fix for a daily screen-time argument, and the health claim gives them something to forward or debate. 99 comments against 136K views suggests it was shared and saved more than discussed.
why_it_worked: 136,020 views vs an account median of 9,832 (13.8x outlier) on a very short clip with the whole instruction readable in about 7 s.
Like rate 0.99% is above the paid-promo range, so the lift looks organic; the topic (a child who always asks for cartoons) is a daily pain point for the audience.
A recognisable kids' character on screen from frame 0 plus a clear, named expert niche (the account name states speech-language pathologist) gives the claim authority without any talking head.
paid_signal: no, like_rate_pct 0.99 is well above 0.3, so nothing points to paid reach.

solo_route.how: 1) Screen-record or film a phone or TV once, locked off, showing the real tap path. 2) In CapCut stack three text bubbles (white rounded boxes with an emoji arrow each) timed one per tap, then a check-mark bubble with the one-line benefit, then a pointer arrow sticker. 3) Put the full steps and caveats in the caption, and end with 'full details below'. 4) Use your own footage or LumeBook book pages instead of a licensed cartoon.
solo_route.needs: A barter early-childhood expert or speech-language pathologist to supply or vouch for any developmental claim, since a 24-year-old non-parent has no credibility on 'better for the child's brain'. Nothing else.

lumebook_version.hook_he: הילד מבקש עוד פרק? לפני שלוחצים פליי, תעשו את זה
lumebook_version.concept: An 8 to 12 second one-take text-on-b-roll clip with three stacked steps for a screen-to-story swap (for example, pausing the cartoon and opening your child's own LumeBook preview) with the developmental claim supplied by a barter expert and the full explanation in the caption.

evidence_notes: Observed: all on-screen Hebrew and the TV scenes. The transcript is a single line, 'תודה רבה.' (Thank you very much) spanning 0 to 11.5 s; this is almost certainly a Whisper filler over music or silence, so there is no usable speech transcript and I cannot say whether there is voice, music or sound. The caption says the setting is in the YouTube app; the TV UI itself is too small to confirm the app, and the speed list values are not legible. The claim 'slower content = healthier for brain and attention' is the creator's assertion, not something the video shows; the caption itself hedges that human, slow content is most recommended. Duration 11.5 s per frames/index.json. The first frame has no text; the hook text begins at about 1 s.
